Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: final full-bleed background plate for an immersive personal website, wide 16:9 landscape.
Create an original airport terminal interior that unmistakably has the art direction and craft of Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse, a richly painted feature-animation film environment, NOT a printed comic and absolutely NOT a low-poly Roblox/game level.
Camera: dynamic wide 24mm cinematic shot from high in a huge international airport atrium, looking diagonally down the terminal. Extremely strong layered depth, monumental curved steel and glass ribs sweeping overhead, a foreground diagonal architectural beam entering the upper right, tapering concourses and a small distant check-in hall. Tall windows on the right look out onto a dense futuristic Toronto-inspired city at sunset. A few small believable painted travelers and suitcases far below provide scale. Leave the centre-right airspace clear for a separately animated character. The left third is a deliberate quieter indigo architectural mass for large opening captions.
Materials: sculpted believable structural depth and accurate perspective, hand-painted angular planes of light, tactile dark steel, brushy reflections on polished stone, dense architectural craft, tiny scratched edge accents, selective hand-drawn contours and stipple only in shadow transitions. Avoid toy blocks and flat featureless walls. Warm golden-amber sunlight rakes across the floor and catches steel edges; saturated cyan bounced light, rich midnight navy and violet shadows, very restrained red registration at out-of-focus contours. Contrast like a dramatic movie still, clear silhouettes, atmospheric falloff, crisp midground and softly painted distant city.
No protagonist or superhero in the image. No text, captions, logos, watermark, panel borders, artificial HUD, neon synthwave gradients, checkerboard, or uniform halftone overlay. Full frame opaque finished production painting, not a mockup. Composition must feel genuinely cinematic and spatial, not a frontal architectural brochure.

Use case: stylized-concept. Final cinematic wide 16:9 environment painting for a website scene.
An original airport CHECK-IN hall in the unmistakable visual language of Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse. Rich high-end feature-animation background painting, sculpted architectural volume, strong perspective, painted angular lighting planes, broken ink contours, selective shadow hatching, tactile reflected light. Not a photo, not low-poly, not a Roblox set, not flat vector.
Eye-level 35mm composed movie shot, looking diagonally across a beautiful contemporary international-airport check-in counter. A single curved deep-indigo counter with warm brushed brass trim dominates the RIGHT HALF of the scene, extending toward distant desks and vanishing point. Behind it: two believable painted airline staff handling luggage labels and a long baggage belt carrying a few different textured suitcases into a recessed opening. A restrained overhead navy departure board with mostly dark unreadable dot-matrix rows. Small ordinary queue stanchions, a traveler handing over a passport, a thoughtful believable layout. Deep layered terminal ceiling beams and amber recessed lights; tall glass to the far right lets golden sunset stripes rake across polished stone. No other terminal scene visible beyond this room. The LEFT THIRD is a darker, calm close architectural column and floor, kept clear for a short caption.
Palette: deep ink navy / muted teal structural shadows, golden amber warm light, cream stone, subtle red/orange bounced edge accents. Surface paint strokes visible at edges, a few hand-drawn offset cyan contours. No broad blank magenta walls, neon/synthwave, uniform dots or crude shapes. Believable materials, layered production-design details and atmospheric depth. Dramatic but sophisticated: a real place inside a beautifully art-directed animated film.
No foreground hero, no giant readable signage, no corporate airline brands, no invented words, no UI panel, no title, no watermark or border. Original scene, not a reproduction of an existing movie shot.

Use case: stylized-concept. A finished wide 16:9 cinematic background painting for a personal website.
An original airport security checkpoint in the recognizable visual language and production craft of Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse. Tactile hand-painted 3D volumes, decisive angular planes of light, broken ink contours, nuanced shadow stipple, rich realistic materials and believable architecture, never low-poly/Roblox, never flat vector or a comic-book panel.
Shot from passenger eye level approaching a security lane at a slightly diagonal angle. In the RIGHT HALF, a continuous textured brushed-steel conveyor leads through a substantial dark teal X-ray machine. Several grey security trays and one red backpack sit on the belt. A traveler is naturally taking a laptop out of a bag, an airport officer stands beside the lane, and a few people queue behind. A large dark unlit widescreen inspection monitor is angled very slightly toward camera on the right, with an empty navy screen reserved for a separately placed project image. Everything has credible scale, detailed construction and a clear path through the arch.
Huge curved terminal roof ribs continue overhead, dark navy metal and warm cream stone, amber practical lights and cool cyan side light, sunset reflections on the floor. Deep layered room; next terminal area obscured by actual architecture. The LEFT THIRD is a darker calm architectural foreground with space for short captions. It must feel like the next shot of the same exquisitely painted airport movie: golden light, indigo-violet shadows, small warm red accents.
No title, UI, logos, invented words, large text, watermark, borders, or hero character. No futuristic sci-fi scanning beams or laser traps; recognizable everyday airport security, made cinematic through camera, painterly lighting, texture and composition. Original scene, not a copied film shot.
